sentences.en: Not to get mad because they raided me.

sentences.en: Okay, this is what y'all do.

sentences.zh: 在地下蛰伏 20 年后，

sentences.en: Something really unexpected thrust Dapper Dan back into the spotlight.
sentences.zh: 一件意想不到的事情让 Dapper Dan 重回聚光灯下。

sentences.en: It was May of 2017, when Gucci sent a jacket down the runway for their cruise collection.
sentences.zh: 那是 2017 年 5 月，Gucci 在其早春度假系列秀场上推出了一件夹克。

sentences.en: It was a very distinctive jacket, with a black fur torso and huge puffy leather balloon sleeves covered in G's.
sentences.zh: 那是一件非常有辨识度的夹克，黑色皮草衣身，配上巨大的皮革泡泡袖，上面印满了 G 字母。

sentences.en: This jacket looked almost exactly like a design Dan made back in the 80s.
sentences.zh: 这件夹克看起来几乎和 Dan 在 80 年代设计的作品一模一样。

sentences.en: Really, like, identical.
sentences.zh: 真的，简直一模一样。

sentences.en: If you look at the images of Dapper Dan's original and Gucci's version of the jacket,
sentences.zh: 如果你对比一下 Dapper Dan 的原作和 Gucci 的版本，

sentences.en: Gucci very obviously and directly knocked him off.
sentences.zh: Gucci 很明显直接抄袭了他。

sentences.en: A hundred percent definitely.
sentences.zh: 百分之百确定。

sentences.en: And unlike what Dapper Dan had been doing,
sentences.zh: 而且与 Dapper Dan 过去的做法不同，

sentences.en: Gucci wasn't remixing something old into something new.
sentences.zh: Gucci 并不是在把旧元素重组成新设计。

sentences.en: They just made an exact replica.
sentences.zh: 他们只是做了一个完全的复制品。

sentences.en: And while Gucci could call the federal marshals on Dapper Dan,
sentences.zh: 虽然 Gucci 可以叫联邦法警去抓 Dapper Dan，

sentences.en: Dapper Dan didn't have that option.
sentences.zh: 但 Dapper Dan 却没有这种选择权。

sentences.en: And it was not because Gucci is big and Dapper Dan is small.
sentences.zh: 这并不是因为 Gucci 大而 Dapper Dan 小。

sentences.en: It's because what Gucci did is perfectly legal.
sentences.zh: 而是因为 Gucci 的做法完全合法。

sentences.en: The design in the American system is fully copyable.
sentences.zh: 在美国体系下，服装设计是可以被完全复制的。

sentences.en: Gucci wasn't copying a two-dimensional image.
sentences.zh: Gucci 抄的不是二维图像。

sentences.en: It wasn't a logo or a pattern.
sentences.zh: 那不是标志或图案。

sentences.en: They were copying the design of the garment, the shape and the cut and the material.
sentences.zh: 他们抄袭的是服装的设计，包括廓形、剪裁和材质。

sentences.en: And you can totally just do that.
sentences.zh: 而你完全可以这样做。

sentences.en: The American fashion industry is very, very successful.
sentences.zh: 美国时尚产业非常、非常成功。

sentences.en: It makes a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 它赚了很多钱。

sentences.en: It's worldwide in its reach.
sentences.zh: 它的影响力遍布全球。

sentences.en: It's done very well over the last few decades.
sentences.zh: 过去几十年里它发展得非常好。

sentences.en: And yet the core idea, the design, can be copied by anyone and is copied by anyone.
sentences.zh: 然而，其核心理念——设计，却可以被任何人抄袭，也确实被任何人抄袭着。

sentences.en: If you come up with a cool sleeve or a really different looking collar, you have no claim to it in the American copyright system.
sentences.zh: 如果你设计出一款很酷的袖子或非常独特的领子，在美国版权法下，你没有任何权利主张。

sentences.en: If you come up with something that's useful or technologically innovative,
sentences.zh: 如果你发明了某种实用或技术创新的东西，

sentences.en: like maybe it's a new kind of sweat-wicking fabric, maybe you could get a patent.
sentences.zh: 比如一种新型的排汗面料，那你或许能申请专利。

sentences.en: In theory, like a unique kind of toggle could be patented.
sentences.zh: 理论上，一种独特的扣子是可以申请专利的。

sentences.en: You know, it has to be non-obvious and novel.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它必须是非显而易见且具有创新性的。

sentences.en: It's a much higher hurdle to get a patent.
sentences.zh: 申请专利的门槛要高得多。

sentences.en: But otherwise, no.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，不行。

sentences.en: All designs are fair game.
sentences.zh: 所有设计都是公平竞争的对象。

sentences.en: The argument for this lack of regulation is that it keeps the fashion cycle churning.
sentences.zh: 支持这种监管缺失的论点是，它能让时尚周期不断循环。

sentences.en: After all, a trend means a thing that everyone is copying.

sentences.en: New styles proliferate and spread, and we all go out shopping.

sentences.en: Yes, so what copying does is enable the fashion cycle,
sentences.zh: 是的，所以抄袭的作用是推动时尚周期，

sentences.en: so the cycle of something coming into fashion and going out,
sentences.zh: 也就是让某种东西流行起来又过时的周期，

sentences.en: it enables that to move more quickly.
sentences.zh: 它让这个周期运转得更快。

sentences.en: Kyle Rustiala and his co-author Chris Sprigman make this argument
sentences.zh: Kyle Rustiala 和他的合著者 Chris Sprigman 在书中提出了这个观点，

sentences.en: in their book, The Knockoff Economy.
sentences.zh: 书名是《仿冒经济》。

sentences.en: In fashion, everyone copies each other all the time because the clothing industry runs on a fuel concocted of desire and trend proliferation.
sentences.zh: 在时尚界，每个人都在不停地互相抄袭，因为服装业的燃料是由欲望和潮流扩散混合而成的。

sentences.en: You might buy a new phone every few years because the technology improves, but shirts generally don't get better at shirting.
sentences.zh: 你可能每隔几年就买一部新手机，因为技术在进步，但衬衫通常不会因为技术进步而变得更“衬衫”。

sentences.en: You consume as your taste changes, and designers have to appeal to what you like and what style is in, and so they steal from each other.
sentences.zh: 你随着品味的改变而消费，设计师必须迎合你的喜好和当下的流行风格，所以他们互相剽窃。

sentences.en: Sometimes people take the view of, like, you know, copying is the ransom of success.
sentences.zh: 有时人们会认为，你知道，抄袭是成功的代价。

sentences.en: And it's a good thing or it's part of the ether.
sentences.zh: 这要么是件好事，要么是时尚氛围的一部分。

sentences.en: We just let it happen.
sentences.zh: 我们只是任由它发生。

sentences.en: It's a little easier when you're a really big company to do that.
sentences.zh: 当你是一家大公司时，这样做会容易一些。

sentences.en: When you're a small firm, it's a little tougher.
sentences.zh: 当你是一家小公司时，情况就艰难多了。

sentences.en: Every couple of years, new legislation is brought forward to make American fashion law more strict.
sentences.zh: 每隔几年，就会有新的立法提案被提出，旨在加强美国时尚法律的严苛程度。

sentences.en: And it always falls through.
sentences.zh: 但总是无疾而终。

sentences.en: And Professor Rastiala argues that the reason is fashion copyright is a double-edged sword.
sentences.zh: Rastiala 教授认为，原因在于时尚版权是一把双刃剑。

sentences.en: If you tighten up the rules to protect independent designers, you also tighten up the rules to protect major fashion houses, who stand to gain far more than they have to lose.
sentences.zh: 如果你收紧规则来保护独立设计师，你同时也收紧了保护大型时装屋的规则，而他们从中获益远多于损失。

sentences.en: He argues that if fashion copyright was written more strictly and or enforced more heavily, it could have odd cultural ripple effects.
sentences.zh: 他认为，如果时尚版权法写得更严格或执行得更严厉，可能会产生奇怪的文化连锁反应。

sentences.en: Well, this is really an idea that I don't want to claim.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这其实不是我想提出的观点。

sentences.en: It's a colleague of ours at NYU, Barton Beebe, who really first talked about this.
sentences.zh: 是我们 NYU 的同事 Barton Beebe 最先谈到这个的。

sentences.en: But sumptuary codes in the past dictated who could wear what.
sentences.zh: 但过去的禁奢令规定了谁能穿什么。

sentences.en: And only certain classes of people could wear certain clothing.
sentences.zh: 只有特定阶层的人才能穿特定的服装。

sentences.en: And stricter fashion law could function like modern sumptuary codes.
sentences.zh: 而更严格的时尚法律可能会像现代的禁奢令一样运作。

sentences.en: In a world with much stricter fashion copyright, if you wanted to wear something new and cool or trendy right now, you couldn't.
sentences.zh: 在一个时尚版权极其严格的世界里，如果你现在想穿点新潮、酷炫的东西，你根本做不到。

sentences.en: Unless you wanted to pay hundreds of dollars for the authentic, trend-setting designer piece.
sentences.zh: 除非你愿意花几百美元去买那些正版的、引领潮流的设计师单品。

sentences.en: Even if you made your own version, if you sewed a particular kind of dress or blouse
sentences.zh: 即使你自己做，如果你缝制了一件特定款式的裙子或衬衫，

sentences.en: inspired by something you saw on Instagram, you could be sued for infringement.
sentences.zh: 灵感来自你在 Instagram 上看到的东西，你都可能被起诉侵权。

sentences.en: And so one of the great things about the freedom to copy that we currently have
sentences.zh: 所以，我们目前拥有的这种“抄袭自由”的一大好处在于，

sentences.en: is it enables everyone to wear designs.
sentences.zh: 它让每个人都能穿上这些设计。

sentences.en: So if a really popular design comes out of, let's say, Prada at a very high price point,
sentences.zh: 如果 Prada 出了一款非常受欢迎的设计，价格非常昂贵，

sentences.zh: 普通人，更不用说穷人，根本买不起。

sentences.zh: 但能够仿制这种设计，意味着他们也能穿上那种设计，他们有了接触这些设计的机会。

sentences.en: Although, let's not take a democracy of goods as an actual form of democracy.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们别把这种“商品的民主化”当成真正的民主形式。

sentences.zh: 你知道我们的世界早已被分成了三六九等。

sentences.zh: 头等舱、商务舱和加长空间座位。

sentences.en: Those who can actually afford a $2,000 bag and those who buy them on Canal Street.
sentences.zh: 那些买得起两千美元包包的人，和那些在运河街买仿品的人。

sentences.en: The designers who are big enough to protect their work, and those who aren't.
sentences.zh: 那些大到足以保护自己作品的设计师，和那些做不到的设计师。

sentences.zh: 那你看到他们用你的设计时，生气吗？

sentences.en: No, I expect that.
sentences.zh: 不，我预料到了。

sentences.en: I never, even to this day, I never expect people to play fair.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，我从不指望人们会公平竞争。

sentences.zh: Dapper Dan 本人早已习惯了这种不公。

sentences.zh: 但当 Gucci 夹克的照片出现在互联网上时，

sentences.zh: Dapper Dan 几十年来第一次重新成为人们热议的话题。

sentences.zh: 仅仅几个月后，即 2017 年 12 月，他们就联系了 Dapper Dan。

sentences.zh: 他们给 Dan 提供了一个设计师职位，而且给予他完全、绝对的自主权。
